Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1222 PM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

- Warming trend today and Tuesday with highs around 60 degrees 
Tuesday. 

- Rain chances increase late Wednesday into Thursday, with an 
unsettled pattern continuing into the weekend. 

- A much colder airmass arrives Thursday, triggering lake effect 
rain and snow showers late Thursday through Saturday.

&&

.AVIATION...

Marginal MVFR / low-end VFR ceilings continue to mix out across the 
Thumb Region this afternoon, with MBS/FNT/PTK/DET now west of the 
remaining stratus. These ceilings will continue to erode through 
this afternoon, with high clouds streaming in from the northwest. 
Northwest winds will back this afternoon and evening, becoming 
southwesterly by/around 00Z as high pressure to our south crests the 
region. Late tonight through Tuesday, low pressure will track east 
across Ontario and into Quebec, sending a dry cold front across 
southeast Michigan. Along the front, winds will shift from southwest 
to west-northwest with FROPA expected between 09-12Z Tuesday. Some 
shallow boundary layer moisture lingers into the overnight hours, 
with some guidance hinting at a narrow window for shallow BR to 
develop. This narrow window will rely heavily on the departure of 
overnight mid/high clouds and how much time is left for an uptick in 
nocturnal cooling before/around sunrise.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* None.
